questionText: Choose the sentence with CORRECT subject-verb agreement:
options: A) The committee have made their decision
B) The committee has made its decision
C) Both A and B are correct
D) Neither is correct
explanation: Both sentences are correct. Committee can be treated as singular (British English more commonly uses plural verbs with collective nouns).

questionText: Which sentence uses the SUBJUNCTIVE mood correctly?
options: A) I wish I was taller
B) I wish I were taller
C) I wish I am taller
D) I wish I be taller
explanation: I wish I were taller uses the subjunctive mood correctly. The subjunctive uses were for all persons when expressing wishes or hypothetical situations.

questionText: Identify the DANGLING MODIFIER in the sentence:
options: A) Running through the park the flowers were beautiful
B) She ran through the park and saw beautiful flowers
C) The flowers in the park were beautiful as she ran
D) While running through the park she saw beautiful flowers
explanation: Running through the park has no clear subject - it seems the flowers were running. This is a dangling modifier. Option D correctly attributes the action to she.

questionText: Which sentence demonstrates PARALLEL STRUCTURE correctly?
options: A) She likes swimming hiking and to run
B) She likes to swim to hike and run
C) She likes swimming hiking and running
D) She likes swim hike and running
explanation: Parallel structure requires the same grammatical form for all items in a series. Swimming hiking and running are all gerunds maintaining parallel structure.

questionText: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
options: A) Its a beautiful day isnt it
B) Its a beautiful day is not it
C) It is a beautiful day is it not
D) Its a beautiful day isnt it
explanation: It is a beautiful day is it not is the fully expanded and correctly punctuated form. Contractions would require apostrophes which are not shown in the options.

questionText: Which sentence uses a RESTRICTIVE CLAUSE correctly?
options: A) The book which I borrowed was excellent
B) The book that I borrowed was excellent
C) Both A and B are correct
D) Neither is correct
explanation: That is used in restrictive clauses (essential to the meaning). Which is used in non-restrictive clauses (added information set off by commas). Both are commonly accepted in usage.

questionText: Identify the sentence with a MISPLACED MODIFIER:
options: A) He almost drove his children to school every day
B) He drove his children to school almost every day
C) Almost he drove his children to school every day
D) He drove almost his children to school every day
explanation: He almost drove suggests he nearly drove but did not. The intended meaning is He drove his children to school almost every day - meaning on most days.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the PASSIVE VOICE?
options: A) The report was wrote by her
B) The report was written by her
C) The report written by her
D) The report is write by her
explanation: The report was written by her uses the correct passive construction: was + past participle (written). Was wrote is incorrect - wrote is simple past not past participle.

questionText: Complete the sentence correctly: If I _____ the lottery I would donate to charity.
options: A) win
B) won
C) have won
D) had won
explanation: Won is correct for a second conditional hypothetical situation. If I won (simple past) expresses an unlikely or imagined scenario. Had won would require would have donated.

questionText: Which sentence contains a SPLIT INFINITIVE?
options: A) She decided to quickly leave the room
B) She quickly decided to leave the room
C) She decided to leave the room quickly
D) Quickly she decided to leave the room
explanation: A split infinitive has an adverb inserted between to and the verb. To quickly leave splits the infinitive to leave. While acceptable in modern usage it is traditionally avoided.

questionText: Choose the correctly written CONDITIONAL sentence:
options: A) Had I known I would have come earlier
B) If I would have known I would have come earlier
C) If I knew I would have come earlier
D) Had I know I would have come earlier
explanation: Had I known I would have come earlier is a third conditional with inverted subject-auxiliary. It means If I had known I would have come earlier. The inversion of Had and I is formal but correct.

questionText: Identify the INDEPENDENT CLAUSE in this sentence: Although it was raining they continued playing.
options: A) Although it was raining
B) they continued playing
C) Although it was raining they continued
D) it was raining they continued playing
explanation: They continued playing is the independent clause - it can stand alone as a complete sentence. Although it was raining is a dependent subordinate clause.

questionText: Which sentence uses REPORTED SPEECH correctly?
options: A) She said that she is coming
B) She said that she was coming
C) She told that she is coming
D) She said that she will come
explanation: She said that she was coming uses backshifted tense correctly in reported speech. The present tense is coming becomes past tense was coming.

questionText: Choose the sentence with CORRECT punctuation for a compound sentence:
options: A) She studied hard therefore she passed
B) She studied hard, therefore, she passed
C) She studied hard therefore, she passed
D) She studied hard; therefore she passed
explanation: A semicolon before a conjunctive adverb like therefore is correct. She studied hard; therefore she passed. A comma can also follow therefore.

questionText: Which sentence avoids a COMMA SPLICE?
options: A) I was tired, I went to sleep
B) I was tired so I went to sleep
C) I was tired, so, I went to sleep
D) I was tired; I, went to sleep
explanation: I was tired so I went to sleep correctly joins two clauses with the coordinating conjunction so. A comma splice incorrectly joins two independent clauses with only a comma.

questionText: Complete the sentence: She has been living in Mumbai _____ 2010.
options: A) for
B) since
C) from
D) during
explanation: Since is used with a specific point in time (2010) when using perfect tenses. For is used with a duration of time.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an APPOSITIVE?
options: A) My sister, a doctor, works at the hospital
B) My sister a doctor works at the hospital
C) My sister a doctor, works at the hospital
D) My sister, a doctor works at the hospital
explanation: An appositive phrase (a doctor) renames the noun (my sister) and must be set off by commas on both sides when it is non-essential information.

questionText: Choose the sentence with CORRECT use of WHOM:
options: A) Who did you speak to?
B) Whom did you speak to?
C) To who did you speak?
D) Whom spoke to you?
explanation: Whom is correct as the object of the preposition to. You spoke to whom. Whom replaces him/her. Who replaces he/she.

questionText: Identify the ELLIPTICAL CLAUSE: She runs faster than I.
options: A) She runs faster
B) than I
C) than I (run) - the verb is omitted
D) She runs
explanation: An elliptical clause omits words understood from context. Than I is an elliptical clause where (run) is omitted. The full form would be She runs faster than I run.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the FUTURE PERFECT tense?
options: A) She will finish the project tomorrow
B) She will have finished the project by tomorrow
C) She would finish the project by tomorrow
D) She has finished the project tomorrow
explanation: The future perfect (will have + past participle) expresses an action that will be completed before a future point. She will have finished by tomorrow is correct.

questionText: Which sentence is grammatically CORRECT?
options: A) Between you and I this is a secret
B) Between you and me this is a secret
C) Between you and myself this is a secret
D) Between I and you this is a secret
explanation: Between you and me is correct. The preposition between requires object pronouns (me not I). Between you and I is a common hypercorrection.

questionText: Complete the sentence correctly: The data _____ been analyzed.
options: A) has
B) have
C) Both A and B can be correct
D) is
explanation: Data is the plural of datum. Traditionally the data have been analyzed is correct. However in modern usage the data has become widely accepted treating data as singular.

questionText: Which sentence uses an ABSOLUTE PHRASE correctly?
options: A) The game ending we went home
B) The game having ended we went home
C) Having end the game we went home
D) The game was ended and we went home
explanation: The game having ended we went home uses an absolute phrase correctly. An absolute phrase has a noun and a participial phrase and modifies the entire main clause.

questionText: Choose the sentence with CORRECT use of FEWER vs LESS:
options: A) There are less students today
B) There are fewer students today
C) There is fewer students today
D) There are less students then usual
explanation: Fewer is used with countable nouns (students). Less is used with uncountable nouns. There are fewer students today is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a NEGATIVE INVERSION for emphasis?
options: A) Never I have seen such courage
B) Never have I seen such courage
C) I never have seen such courage
D) Have never I seen such courage
explanation: Never have I seen uses negative inversion correctly. When a negative adverb begins a sentence the auxiliary verb precedes the subject for emphasis.

questionText: Complete the sentence: He spoke as if he _____ the answer.
options: A) knows
B) knew
C) known
D) know
explanation: Knew is correct after as if in a hypothetical situation (subjunctive/unreal conditional). As if followed by a verb uses the past tense for unreal situations.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a SEMICOLON?
options: A) She loves reading; and she also enjoys writing
B) She loves reading; she also enjoys writing
C) She loves reading, she also enjoys writing
D) She loves reading; but also enjoys writing
explanation: She loves reading; she also enjoys writing correctly uses a semicolon to join two independent clauses. A semicolon should not be followed by and or but.

questionText: Identify the TAUTOLOGY in these sentences:
options: A) She returned back to school
B) She returned to school
C) She went back to school
D) She went to school again
explanation: Returned back is a tautology - returned already means came back so adding back is redundant. She returned to school is the correct non-redundant form.

questionText: Which sentence uses the GERUND correctly as a subject?
options: A) To swim is excellent exercise
B) Swimming is excellent exercise
C) Swim is excellent exercise
D) Swam is excellent exercise
explanation: Swimming (gerund) as a subject is perfectly correct. Both swimming (gerund) and to swim (infinitive) can serve as subjects though gerunds are more natural.

questionText: Complete the sentence correctly: She suggested _____ earlier.
options: A) to leave
B) leave
C) leaving
D) left
explanation: Suggest is followed by a gerund (ing form). She suggested leaving earlier is correct. Suggest is not followed by an infinitive.

questionText: Which sentence uses INVERSION after so correctly?
options: A) She was tired and so was I
B) She was tired and so I was
C) She was tired and so am I
D) She was tired and I so was
explanation: And so was I correctly uses inversion after so to agree with a past tense statement. The auxiliary verb (was) precedes the subject (I).

questionText: Identify the PLEONASM in these phrases:
options: A) Adequate enough
B) Completely adequate
C) Mostly adequate
D) Fairly adequate
explanation: Adequate enough is a pleonasm (redundancy). Adequate already means sufficient or enough so adding enough is redundant.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS tense?
options: A) She had been working for five hours when he arrived
B) She has been working for five hours when he arrived
C) She was working for five hours when he arrived
D) She would have been working for five hours when he arrived
explanation: Had been working is the past perfect continuous correctly expressing an ongoing action that continued up to a past point.

questionText: Choose the sentence that AVOIDS a dangling participle:
options: A) Having finished the exam he left
B) Having finished the exam the teacher dismissed him
C) The exam finished and he left
D) Finishing the exam left him tired
explanation: Having finished the exam he left correctly links the participial phrase to the subject he. In option B having finished seems to refer to the teacher.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses NEITHER...NOR?
options: A) Neither she nor I are going
B) Neither she nor I is going
C) Neither she nor I were going
D) Neither she nor I am going
explanation: With neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject. I is closest so the verb should be am. However formal grammar often uses is here. Neither she nor I is going is the standard formal choice.

questionText: Complete the sentence: The more you practice _____ you become.
options: A) better
B) the best
C) the better
D) more better
explanation: The more...the better is a parallel comparative structure. The more you practice the better you become. Both parts use the comparative form.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a CONDITIONAL PERFECT?
options: A) If she had studied she would pass
B) If she had studied she would have passed
C) If she studied she would have passed
D) If she studies she would have passed
explanation: The third conditional uses if + past perfect and would have + past participle. If she had studied she would have passed expresses an unreal past condition.

questionText: Identify the CORRECT use of a COLON:
options: A) I need: milk eggs and bread
B) I need the following: milk eggs and bread
C) I need milk: eggs and bread
D) I: need milk eggs and bread
explanation: A colon is correctly used after a complete independent clause to introduce a list. I need the following is a complete clause so the colon before the list is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses EMPHASIS with an auxiliary verb?
options: A) She do love painting
B) She does love painting
C) She doing love painting
D) She is love painting
explanation: She does love painting uses the emphatic do construction correctly. The auxiliary does emphasizes the main verb love and the main verb returns to base form.

questionText: Which sentence avoids an AMBIGUOUS pronoun reference?
options: A) When Jane met Mary she was nervous
B) Jane was nervous when she met Mary
C) She was nervous when Jane met Mary
D) When meeting Mary Jane she was nervous
explanation: Jane was nervous when she met Mary clearly establishes Jane as the subject making the pronoun she unambiguous. In option A she could refer to either Jane or Mary.

questionText: Complete the sentence: It is essential that he _____ the rules.
options: A) follow
B) follows
C) followed
D) is following
explanation: After expressions like it is essential that the subjunctive mood requires the base form of the verb without s. It is essential that he follow (not follows) is correct.

questionText: Which sentence uses FRONTING for emphasis correctly?
options: A) This book I have already read
B) I this book have already read
C) This I book have already read
D) Read this book I have already
explanation: This book I have already read uses fronting correctly. Moving the object (this book) to the front of the sentence creates emphasis.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses WHOM in a relative clause?
options: A) The man who I spoke to was helpful
B) The man whose I spoke to was helpful
C) The man whom I spoke to was helpful
D) The man which I spoke to was helpful
explanation: Whom is correct as the object of the preposition to in the relative clause. The man (whom I spoke to) - whom replaces him.

questionText: Choose the sentence with CORRECT use of a GERUND after a preposition:
options: A) She succeeded in to complete the project
B) She succeeded in completing the project
C) She succeeded in complete the project
D) She succeeded in completed the project
explanation: After a preposition (in) we use a gerund (completing) not an infinitive. She succeeded in completing the project is correct.

questionText: Which sentence uses ANAPHORA (repetition for effect) as a rhetorical device?
options: A) We shall fight on the beaches we shall fight on the landing grounds we shall fight in the fields
B) We shall fight everywhere including beaches and landing grounds
C) The fight will continue on all fronts
D) Everywhere we will continue fighting
explanation: We shall fight on the beaches we shall fight on the landing grounds we shall fight in the fields uses anaphora - the repetition of we shall fight at the beginning of successive clauses for rhetorical effect. This is from Churchill famous speech.

questionText: Complete: She _____ for two hours when the lights went out.
options: A) studied
B) has been studying
C) had been studying
D) was studying
explanation: Had been studying is the past perfect continuous expressing an ongoing action that was happening before another past event (lights going out).

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses CLEFT SENTENCE construction?
options: A) It is John who broke the window
B) It was John who breaks the window
C) It is John which broke the window
D) It was that John broke the window
explanation: It is John who broke the window is a cleft sentence that places emphasis on John. Cleft sentences use It is/was + focused element + relative clause.
